chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: Back with Charlie Johnson at Small's, and leaving a band properly
summary: Off and on 18 months to two years; musicians took weeks off for other gigs and Caldwell never left a band cold.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, that's progress. Well, now, after Elmer Snowden, they say Charlie Johnson again. Well, that was still at Small's.
Well, how long were you there?
Well, off and on about 18 months or

two years, because you -- if a guy had a job, you know, sometimes five days, have a job here at this club, maybe about three or four months, get some (unintelligible) and go back to the other fellow, and because they picked the fellows they want because -- to strengthen the band, a section or something like that. They didn't care too much for those -- (unintelligible) able capab ones, they came aboard (unintelligible).
I mean would you take off sometimes during that time?
You'd go -- some other gig would come up, and you could take off a couple of weeks.
Yeah, you could take off a couple of weeks, maybe a month.

Yes, definitely. But I never just leave a band cold turkey. (Unintelligible) we going to move, say, if you quit, quit in the right way. (Unintelligible) you someday he might want to come back, and it was very true about that.
Well now, these two bands, Charlie Johnson's and Elmer Snowden's, now, these were very good bands at this time, were they not?
